title: Strings
instructions: A string is just a row of letters — an array of char, with a hidden 'stop' mark at the end that C adds for you.
char name[] = "Sam"; makes a string you can print with %s.
Because a string is really an array, you can reach one letter with an index: name[0] is 'S'.
You can even change a letter: name[0] = 'P' turns "Sam" into "Pam".
Single quotes 'S' = one character. Double quotes "Sam" = a whole string. Different things!
task: Change the first letter so the program prints:  Pam
hint:
Set index 0 to the character 'P' (single quotes):

    name[0] = 'P';
